Looking at the two premises:

1. (P ∧ Q)
2. ¬(P ∧ Q)

These two statements are direct contradictions of each other. Statement 1 asserts that (P ∧ Q) is true, while statement 2 asserts that (P ∧ Q) is false.

By conjunction introduction, combining both premises gives us the contradiction:

(P ∧ Q) ∧ ¬(P ∧ Q)

<answer>(P ∧ Q) ∧ ¬(P ∧ Q)</answer>
